A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching central theorems and transformer construction. Their text, equations, references, and v2's Table 1 and Appendices A–C are readable and support a reliable comparison. V1 has no appendices.

before.justification: V1 presents mathematical constructions and proofs, with no original experiments, empirical simulations, or data analyses. References to LLM capabilities and benchmarks are background.

after.justification: V2 and its appendices remain theoretical. Table 1 compares theoretical resource requirements, and Section 4 explicitly leaves empirical validation for future work.

M1.justification: The single-layer, single-head transformer, token embeddings, transition network, and attention construction are retained. Equation (2) is rewritten equivalently using relative distances. Appendix B supplies a proof of the supporting simulation theorem rather than changing the transformer procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts task evaluations. References to mathematical proofs, games, and reasoning problems illustrate theoretical applicability rather than added evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. V2's Table 1 and expanded literature discussion compare theoretical constructions, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures. The theoretical resource assumptions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case studies. V2's appendices add proof and literature material rather than such analyses.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, and significance tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries to revise or extend. The central theoretical bounds remain unchanged; v2's new comparison table summarizes theoretical requirements of existing constructions.

T1.justification: V1 states Theorem 2 with citations and a short cyclic-queue intuition. V2 adds Appendix B's constructive proof, including a delayed-append register, marked alphabet, simulation invariant, left/right update procedures, and runtime analysis. This substantially expands the mathematical justification for the retained O(t(n)s(n)) simulation bound, while the main theorem statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, Turing-completeness claim, and WINDOW[s(n)] = SPACE[s(n)] characterization are retained. New introductory Remarks 2–3 add an explicit claim that the result justifies engineering strategies based on longer contexts and answers model-size objections for deductive reasoning.

C2.justification: V1's conclusion only proposes improving simulation efficiency. V2 substantially expands the limitations discussion to nonstandard positional encodings, dependence on a known space bound, unresolved learnability, and absent empirical validation. Remark 5 also adds an explanation connecting unique-token attention to constant precision and contrasting it with earlier constructions.

D1.justification: The specified transformer parameters and symbolic construction remain unchanged, and neither version provides code, implementation resources, hardware information, or training details. Appendix B adds mathematical proof details rather than a computational implementation or reproduction protocol.

R1.justification: V2 adds Table 1 and Appendix A to compare prior constructions' resource requirements and architectural modifications. Section 1.2 newly discusses Schuurmans et al.'s related Post-machine approach, contrasting its stated Θ(s(n)^3) cost per TM step with this work's O(s(n)). Additional references and revised sourcing for Theorem 2 further expand the research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. V2 adds explanatory remarks, expands the conclusion into labeled discussion points, and presents single-head notation in Section 2.3 while moving the existing multi-head definition to Appendix C. The Liu-to-Li citation correction refers to the same work.

P2.justification: V2 adds the theoretical comparison Table 1, changes construction-step labels to underlined formatting, and relocates the multi-head equations to Appendix C. The basic page design remains similar, and neither version contains figures.

improvement.justification: Appendix B makes the supporting simulation argument easier to check, while Table 1, the expanded related work, and Section 4 improve positioning and clarify practical limitations. The central theorem and construction remain unchanged. These gains are tempered by a new explanatory error in Remark 5: it calls the hardmax input one-hot, whereas Equation (5) gives scores containing both 2 and 1; the attention output is one-hot.
